To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed a novel radar measurement model for tracking vehicles of rectangular shape in arbitrary scenarios, which allows the tracking of the kinematic and geometric state of the vehicle and is based on the Doppler information of the radar.

we developed a direct scattering model for extended object tracking with high-resolution radar sensors that is applicable to arbitrary traffic scenarios and allows to track the geometric state in addition to the kinematics of objects.

the presented direct scattering model is able to track vehicles with high resolution radars in arbitrary traffic scenarios, that the model allows to determine the kinematic as well as the geometric state of objects, that it does neither require measurement preprocessing, data association nor data clustering, and that the RBPF is able to track the objects using this model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a direct measurement model for tracking vehicles of arbitrary shape in arbitrary traffic situations.
a direct scattering model that is able to track vehicles with high-resolution radar sensors in arbitrary traffic scenarios.
the development of a novel radar measurement model for the tracking of vehicles in arbitrary traffic scenarios, including the geometric state of objects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the measurement model and the RBPF proposed in this paper are suitable for tracking vehicles with radar sensors in arbitrary traffic scenarios, including parallel and cross-traffic.
the proposed approach allows to track the kinematic state of the object as well as its geometric state.
the proposed model is able to track vehicles with high resolution radars and that it is a promising candidate for tracking vehicles in arbitrary scenarios.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a novel measurement model for tracking vehicles in arbitrary traffic scenarios.
we developed a novel radar based measurement model that is able to track objects with a complex geometry.
the measurement model is based on the direct scattering model and the particle filter is based on the Rao-Blackwellised particle filter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple and robust tracking algorithm is possible by using a direct measurement model for high-resolution radar data.

the presented measurement model is able to track vehicles in arbitrary traffic scenarios and to estimate their shape and orientation, while the RBPF is capable of handling the non-linear measurement model in an efficient manner.
a simple and intuitive measurement model for extended object tracking can be derived from the radar equation.
